sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:64867
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1752 of 2024

Applicant :- Manisha Jha
Opposite Party :- State Of Upand 2 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Vikash Chandra Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Akash Tomar,Atul Verma,G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

The instant anticipatory bail application has come up before this Court vide order dated 5.4.2024
passed by Hon'ble Mr.Justice Krishan Pahal.
2.  Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State, apprised the Court that he has received the instructions, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be finally disposed off.

3. Heard Sri Nitin Sharma, learned Advocate, holding brief of Sri Vikas Chandra Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Akash Tomar, learned counsel for the informant and Dr. S.B.Maurya,
learned AGA-I, for the State.
4. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in FIR/Case Crime No.82 of 2023, under Sections 419,420,467,468 and 471 IPC, Police Station Cantt., District Prayagraj during pendency of the trial.

sentences.text:
5. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and two others and according to the FIR,
applicant along with other accused persons after procuring the fake signature of ex-partner of Global Techno Amarjeet Kaur used the same before this Court.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that from the perusal of the FIR present case it reflects that very casually without any allegation applicant, who is lady, has been made accused in the present matter.
7. He further submits that neither there is any allegation nor any evidence which can show that applicant is the person, who prepared fake signature of Amarjeet Kaur, ex-partner of Global Techno.

8. He further submits that even as per prosecution the alleged fake document was prepared by co-accused Pradeep Sharma, who was brother-in-law of co-accused Diwaker Sharma and same document was used in the bail application of co-accused Diwakar Sharma.

9. He further submits that applicant being co-accused also obtained same document without knowing that it was fake one and also used the same in her Criminal Misc.Anticipatory Application No.2622 of 2023.
10.
He further submits that with a detailed order anticipatory bail application of the applicant in that case was allowed by Coordinate Bench of this Court.

11. He further submits that at the time of her anticipatory bail application learned counsel for the informant, who also appeared in that case did not raise any objection with regard to genuineness of any document.
12.
He further submits that the order passed by this Court has also not been either recalled or has been challenged before Apex Court.

13. He further submits that however, anticipatory bail application of co-accused Pradeep Sharma has been dismissed by this Court vide order dated 12.2.2024 passed in Criminal Misc.Anticipatory Bail Application No. 162 of 2024 but the case of applicant is distinguishable from him as Pradeep Sharma was the person who prepared the fake document/signature of Amarjeet Kaur.

entities.text: Criminal Misc.Anticipatory Bail Application No. 162 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 14. He further submits that applicant is lady.

15. He further submits that apart from the present case, applicant was made accused in a case under Sections 376D and 120B IPC at Case Crime No. 211 of 2022, Police Station Link Road, District Ghaziabad but in that case she has already been released on anticipatory bail by Coordinate Bench of this Court.
16. He further submits that it is a case in which investigation is pending and police is trying to arrest the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that in the present matter considering the allegation, custodial interrogation of applicant is not required, therefore, applicant should be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

18. Per contra, learned AGA and the learned counsel appearing for the informant opposed the prayerfor anticipatory bail and submitted that applicant along with co-accused Diwakar Sharma and Pradeep Sharma used the fake document before this Court in another case but they could not dispute the fact that the allegation of preparation of fake document is not against the applicant rather it was against co-accused Pradeep Sharma.
19. They further could not dispute the fact that however applicant is having criminal history of a case under Sections 376-D and 120B IPC but in this case she has been released on anticipatory bail.
20. They further could not dispute the fact that applicant is a lady and her case is distinguishable from the case of co-accused Pradeep Sharma.
21. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
22. In the FIR of the present case no specific allegation has been levelled against the applicant.

Further, from the record it reflects that co-accused Pradeep Sharma was the person who prepared fake document and, therefore, argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant that however applicant used the alleged fake document in her anticipatory bail application but she was not aware that this document was not genuine cannot be ruled out at this stage.

23. Further, however, anticipatory bail application of co-accused Pradeep Sharma has been dismissed by this Bench vide order dated 12.2.2024 passed in Criminal Misc.Bail Application No.
162 of 2024 but from the perusal of the order dated 12.2.2024 it reflects that as he was the person who prepared fake document and used the same in Anticipatory Bail Application of co-accused Diwakar Sharma, therefore, his anticipatory bail application was dismissed but there is no allegation against the applicant that she prepared fake document, therefore, her case is distinguishable from the case of co-accused Pradeep Sharma.

24. Further, applicant is lady and however, apart from the present case applicant is having criminal history of a case under Sections 376D and 120B IPC but in this case with a detailed order she has been released on anticipatory bail by Coordinate Bench of this Court.

25. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of the trial.
26. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail anticipatory application is allowed.

27. In the event of arrest of the applicant-Manisha Jha involved in the aforesaid case crime number,
shall be released on bail till the conclusion of the trial case on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Presiding Officer/Court concerned with the Manisha Jha vs State Of Upand 2 Others on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180130967/

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

29. It is made clear that the observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
